subject.title: fix(telegram): Allow multi-agent ACP bindings within same account

question: Should Telegram allow multiple simultaneous same-account ACP bindings in one topic, or should same-account binding be an explicit handoff that replaces the prior binding?
rationale: The PR title and body promise independent multi-agent bindings, but the current session-binding API resolves one conversation binding and this branch codifies last-writer-wins, so maintainers need to choose the durable routing model before merge.

options.title: Define multi-binding semantics first
options.body: Pause merge until maintainers define how resolve, delivery, unbind, and labels work when one Telegram topic has multiple active same-account ACP bindings.

options.title: Narrow to same-account handoff
options.body: Accept last-writer-wins as the intended behavior, but update the implementation, tests, PR text, and proof to describe an ownership switch rather than independent bindings.

options.title: Keep single-owner behavior
options.body: Reject the behavior change for now and keep one active binding per Telegram account/topic until a broader binding model is sponsored.

recommendation.title: Define multi-binding semantics first
recommendation.body: Pause merge until maintainers define how resolve, delivery, unbind, and labels work when one Telegram topic has multiple active same-account ACP bindings.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current storage/migration contract and have the strongest verified history on this exact Telegram thread-binding persistence surface.
